intro: The penetration testing service workflow follows the internationally recognized Penetration Testing Execution Standard (PTES), ensuring that every engagement is delivered in a standardized, high-quality manner. The workflow comprises the following 8 phases:

phases.name: Pre-engagement Interactions
phases.desc: Project initiation and preparation: both parties agree on the testing scope and specific test items, and authorization confirmation, personnel, and tooling are finalized.

phases.name: Intelligence Gathering
phases.desc: Open-source information collection, asset mapping, and site structure analysis around the authorized assets, culminating in the penetration testing implementation plan.

phases.name: Threat Modeling
phases.desc: Analysis of business assets and processes, assessment of threat actors and their capabilities, and identification of the primary attack surface and risk paths.

phases.name: Vulnerability Analysis
phases.desc: Correlation analysis of scanner results combined with manual verification, reproduction in a controlled environment, and derivation of analytical conclusions.

phases.name: Exploitation
phases.desc: Based on the analysis results, the optimal attack path is selected to perform low-impact, precise verification and confirm the authenticity of each risk.

phases.name: Post-Exploitation
phases.desc: Within the authorized scope, assessment of lateral movement, privilege escalation, and reachability of sensitive data following successful exploitation.

phases.name: Reporting
phases.desc: Consolidation of vulnerability details, evidence, CVSS scoring, and risk ratings into a deliverable penetration test report.

phases.name: Remediation Support
phases.desc: Working with the client to complete remediation based on the report, and conducting retesting where required to confirm that vulnerabilities are fully closed.
